reviews.review:
I feel like I'm in the minority on this, but EDF 5 might be just a bit too long. I thought 2017 Portable had a good pace at 60 missions but this one is nearly twice the length and there are some big lulls in the campaign. That said there are some positive QOL fixes that Sandlot makes to the formula. The ability to keep a portion of the weapon and armour boxes you pick up is welcome, taking some of the sting out of failing a long mission. There's also the new sprint for Ranger that helps him grab nearby boxes much quicker, though I really wish there had been a "toggle sprint" option. Holding shift isn't too bad, but if you're playing with a controller it can be really uncomfortable. I also liked being able to upgrade weapons, it was always nice to see a rifle I liked get better accuracy or range, making it more effective even if I picked up higher rated gear. 

I wasn't a fan of offline and online progress being separated in this game due to the level completion achievements. The bulk of the achievements come from reaching 100% level completion, however you can't mix and match online playthroughs so if you want to get all of the achievements you need either do everything singleplayer or online. Gear carries over though and I believe playing on Hard or higher will still complete level progress for easier difficulties, but it'd be simpler if the progress was just shared. 

This review sounds more negative than positive, but for the most part Earth Defense Force 5 is easy to recommend. Shooting giant ants or teleportation ships is just as satisfying as ever, and the QOL fixes do make a big difference. I'm hoping the next game is a bit more lean though, or at least adds a bit more variety to the mission types if Sandlot wants to keep a similar length.

Also, 

EDF! EDF! EDF!

12/10 
Would call in an Airstrike on a ant again
